name: Sanghamitra Raiguru / ସଂଘମିତ୍ରା ରାଏଗୁରୁ

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sanghamitra Raiguru writes in Odia and Hindi. Kabita Live’s contributor biography also identifies her as a translator, with work bringing Premchand’s fiction into Odia. Her poems here move between intimate attachment and the pressures placed on women’s voices, allowing tenderness and resistance to occupy the same body of writing.

“Meri Galti Kahan Hai?” challenges the habit of judging a woman poet through her appearance rather than her words. The Odia poems explore another form of freedom: letting someone leave, living through a departure, and finding a self that longing has unsettled. In “Dia”, recurring seasons and festivals accompany an appeal to give others space to live. Elsewhere, thirst, the sea and disguised crocodiles turn desire into a setting where vulnerability and danger must also be recognised.

identity_match: Captured bilingual poems and biography are the narrative basis. Same-name Odisha Sambad interview is a plausible lead; accessible excerpts do not establish a sufficient biographical bridge for importing its claims.
